hypothesis: The parent's candidate tracking is correct (all 10 parent episodes end with every circuit uniquely SOLVED, and the ~580 answers that all four harnesses received on these instances agree with the parent's final tables, so the rule model is not contradicted). Its remaining failure mode is budget: the menu ranks queries by unweighted per-circuit candidate counts and accepts ANY informative query, and the 7B often picks weak or unlisted ones (top-of-menu in only ~1/3 of picks; e.g. B(0,0,0)/B(1,1,1) off-menu, 75/25 splits while 50/50 were listed), which drove parent episodes to 15/18 queries (i209, i236). Simulating the parent's own rule over every world the rules allow shows episodes needing 19-20 queries once NOT gates are present (1 AND/5 OR/2 NOT, i.e. i81's inventory: worst 19 even when the model always takes the top item). Ranking by entropy over joint (A,B,C) assignments and accepting only near-best queries (>= 0.9 x best information) keeps every simulated episode within 18 for inventories (3,3,0),(3,3,1),(1,5,2),(2,4,2),(3,3,2) with a model that picks uniformly among the accepted set. Falsified if, on new instances, episodes end with a circuit still holding more than one candidate at budget exhaustion more often than under the parent.
behavior_changes: Space.candidates(): a table's weight is now the number of joint (A,B,C) assignments it takes part in (product of the other circuits' consistent-set sizes per alive inventory split), instead of the number of alive splits.

_splits(): balance/entropy of a query is computed over those joint weights, so queries are ranked by information about the whole joint hypothesis, not bare per-circuit table counts; each split also carries its weighted share p.

New _good(): only queries carrying >= NEAR_BEST (0.9) of the best query's information are listed in the menu and accepted; the menu line shows the weighted split (e.g. '50% / 50%') next to the table counts so the ordering is legible to the model.

A pick that is informative but weak is re-asked (not sent) with feedback naming its split ('only about 19% / 81%; the listed queries split them more evenly'); the rejected-this-turn list wording is generalized accordingly.
preserved_behaviors: Rule-derived enumeration of every circuit allowed by the inventory, joint coupling through the inventory split, and the relaxed fallback on contradiction are unchanged.

The model writes every query; the harness never chooses one. Malformed / repeated / zero-information / solved-circuit picks are still re-asked with the same per-turn rejection list, and no query known to carry no information is ever sent.

Querying still stops as soon as every circuit has a single candidate; the final phase (numbered candidate picks, consistency repair of the model's 24 bits, as in i228 where the model wrote a constant B) is untouched.
Same MAX_TRIES, temperatures, prompts structure, system prompt and final-guess format.
verification: Read all 10 parent traces: every episode ended with A, B, C SOLVED; no crashes; no relaxed ('?') mode; re-asks cost LLM calls only.
Label-free cross-check: the parent's final tables agree with every answer received by all four harnesses on each instance (0 mismatches over ~580 answers).

Offline simulation over all rule-consistent worlds (sampled up to 400 per inventory) of the parent's selection rule: worst-case queries 15/17/19/19/19/20 for (3,3,0)/(3,3,1)/(1,5,2)/(2,4,2)/(3,3,2)/(3,3,3). With the new ranking + near-best acceptance and a model picking uniformly among accepted queries: worst 15/17/15/17/18, 0 episodes over 18, for (3,3,0)/(3,3,1)/(1,5,2)/(2,4,2)/(3,3,2).

Ran check_b1r1_cand_pilot_strict_b10g3r2_b1r1g0.py (re-run after the final edit, identical output): 10/10 status=ok, parsed_final_guess=True, queries_used 5,9,12,11,10,10,12,12,16,14 (mean 11.1 vs parent 11.1); solver calls <= 18 per episode, at most 1 re-ask per episode, no wasted (None) rounds.

In the new traces every episode ends with all three circuits SOLVED, no relaxed mode, and the final tables are identical to the parent's and consistent with all answers from every harness on that instance (0 mismatches). Every sent query was from the near-best set; the weak-pick feedback fired as intended (e.g. 'B(0, 0, 0) splits ... only about 19% / 81%').
risks: Mean queries on this batch did not drop (11.1 vs 11.1); the gain is in the tail, shown only by simulation, not by the 10 real episodes. i253 still used 16/18 with all-near-best picks (late-stage 20/25/33% splits are inherent to one-bit queries).
Stricter acceptance means more re-asks; if the model repeatedly fails 4 tries a round, the 'wasted' counter could end querying before every circuit is pinned (not observed: max 1 re-ask per episode).

The joint-uniform weighting assumes all rule-consistent joint assignments are equally plausible; if the generator samples structures non-uniformly, the ranking is less than optimal (it still never excludes a consistent table).
(3,3,3) inventories were not simulated with the new rule; with three NOTs the hypothesis space (~75k joint worlds) may still exceed 18 queries in the worst case.
